<p class="page-lead">SEEM develops computational methods for sensing, monitoring, imaging, and interpreting the Earth. Our work links measurements, physical understanding, and reproducible computation.</p>

## Research themes

::: {.feature-grid}
::: {.feature-card}
<div class="feature-number">MONITORING</div>

### Microseismicity

Methods for detecting, characterizing, and locating small seismic events, with attention to reliable decisions from noisy observations.

**Topics:** event detection · localization · monitoring
:::

::: {.feature-card}
<div class="feature-number">SENSING</div>

### DAS & VSP

Signal processing and learning methods for distributed acoustic sensing and vertical seismic profile data.

**Topics:** DAS · VSP · denoising
:::

::: {.feature-card}
<div class="feature-number">COMPUTATION</div>

### Scientific ML

Neural operators and physics-informed learning for geophysical inverse problems and reconstruction.

**Topics:** FNO · PINO · inverse problems
:::

::: {.feature-card}
<div class="feature-number">INTERPRETATION</div>

### Explainable geoscience

Reconstruction and explainable-AI tools that support transparent interpretation of the subsurface.

**Topics:** xAI · geological sections · uncertainty
:::
:::

## How the themes connect

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
  A[Earth observations] --> B[Signal processing]
  B --> C[Physical + learned models]
  C --> D[Images and event estimates]
  D --> E[Transparent interpretation]
  E -. informs .-> A
```

This diagram is rendered by Quarto from editable text. It is a useful pattern for students documenting a method without maintaining a separate drawing file.

::: {.callout-note}
## Editorial status

These themes are based on the public SEEM software footprint and the website prototype. Research leads should approve the terminology and add representative figures before launch.
:::

## A reproducible example

The [Python notebook demo](examples/python.qmd) shows how a technical result can live alongside the group website: executable code, a cross-referenced figure, a computed table, and a citation in one reviewable `.qmd` file.
